WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh's daughter, and brought her into the city of David." 1 Kings 3:1

"Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire, and slain the Canaanites that dwelt in the city, and given it for a present unto his daughter, Solomon's wife." 1 Kings 9:16
The Pharaoh of Hadad's day gave the Edomite prince a house, food and land, and gave him "the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen". 1 Kings 11:18–19
When Hadad asked to go home, Pharaoh said, "But what hast thou lacked with me?" 1 Kings 11:21–22
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Chronicles: Solomon would not let his Egyptian wife live in the house of David, "because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come". 2 Chronicles 8:11
Kings names "the daughter of Pharaoh" first among the "strange women" Solomon loved. 1 Kings 11:1–2
Solomon rebuilt Gezer, the city Pharaoh had given as a present. 1 Kings 9:16–17
A marriage alliance: "Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt". 1 Kings 3:1
Solomon's merchants brought horses and chariots out of Egypt, and passed them on to the kings of the Hittites and of Syria. 1 Kings 10:28–29 2 Chronicles 1:16–17
Hadad, sheltered in Pharaoh's court, became "an adversary unto Solomon". 1 Kings 11:14

DATES DIFFER

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No name and no years; any date depends on which king he was (see below).
Psusennes (Pasebkhanu) II, last of the 21st dynasty
W. M. F. Petrie (1915); earlier Winer and Ewald, as reported by C. F. Keil (1872)

Petrie gives Pasebkhanu II 987–952 BC and the marriage about 970; he adds that Hadad was first received by Siamen and married the queen's sister probably under Pasebkhanu. Keil reports Winer and Ewald for Psusennes, reasoning back from Shishak, who began the next dynasty. 1 Kings 3:1 1 Kings 11:40 [9][39]
Psinaches, the king before Psusennes
J. R. Lumby (1886)
Since Manetho gives Psusennes II only fourteen years, "it seems more probable that the princess whom Solomon married was the daughter of Psinaces who preceded Psusennes". 1 Kings 3:1 [37]
A late king of the 21st dynasty, not yet identifiable
The Pulpit Commentary, after R. S. Poole
Because Shishak began the 22nd dynasty, this Pharaoh was a late king of the 21st; but with Manetho's figures in conflict he "cannot yet be identified on Manetho's list". 1 Kings 3:1 [38]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture never gives this king's name, or the name of his daughter.
Scripture does not say whether the Pharaoh who sheltered Hadad in David's day is the Pharaoh whose daughter Solomon married.
Scripture does not say why Pharaoh attacked Gezer.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThe person record joins the Pharaoh whose daughter Solomon married (1 Kgs 3:1; 9:16) with the Pharaoh who sheltered Hadad the Edomite in David's day and made him his brother-in-law (1 Kgs 11:18–22). Scripture calls both only "Pharaoh king of Egypt" and does not say they were one man. 1 Kings 3:1 1 Kings 11:18–22

Scholars' viewTahpenes, called "the queen", is named only in 1 Kings 11:19–20. Ellicott's commentary calls it "a name unknown, either in history or in the Egyptian monuments"; the Pulpit Commentary, after R. S. Poole, says no name like it "has yet been found among those of the period". 1 Kings 11:19 [40][41]
